visual_text: A fall weeks ago can explain new symptoms now
Chronic subdural haematoma: a slow bleed between the brain and the skull
The fall or knock to the head. It may seem minor, or be forgotten.
New unsteadiness or falls, headache, weakness on one side, slower or muddled thinking, drowsiness.
Tell the doctor about the fall. Ask whether a brain scan is needed.
Often treatable. Sudden or severe symptoms: get emergency help.
Shapey et al. 2016; El Rahal et al. 2023; Brennan et al. 2017
alt_text: Illustrative timeline. An older woman sits on her kitchen floor after a fall, hand to her forehead. Weeks later she is tired rising from her armchair: new unsteadiness, headache, one-sided weakness, muddled thinking or drowsiness. At the GP with her son: mention the fall, ask about a scan. A head diagram shows a slow bleed between brain and skull. Often treatable; sudden or severe: emergency help.
